turns.input:
$crumb I'm a solo developer trying to help small commercial embroidery shops in Ontario. I used to schedule production at a friend's shop. Last week two customer orders reached the machine with a blank thread colour or size, so the operator stopped and called the office. About 100 order lines arrive each week as a CSV; a rushed manual skim misses blanks. I want a small sustainable business, and that owner can try a simple local tool on Friday October 9. I have no other customers or interviews, and no application yet. Help me make the first useful test. Don't build or contact anyone yet.

Garment size. The export has order_id, garment_size and thread_colour columns, plus quantity. Blank or whitespace-only size or colour is incomplete; we are not checking whether a filled value is correct. One export is under 100 rows and sometimes has quoted commas. The office person uses a Windows laptop and can open a local browser page, but would not use a terminal. The original CSV must stay untouched. The owner can try it on October 9; nobody outside that shop has agreed. No build or sending yet.
turns.output:
Those two machine stoppages give us a concrete first test: can the office catch missing garment sizes and thread colours before an order reaches production? I’ll prepare Friday’s test and check the business assumptions, while keeping building and outreach on hold.

The broader shop tools cover much more than this check; Printavo lists plans starting at $109/month. A local checker is a plausible small experiment, but a spreadsheet rule is a serious substitute. Friday needs to show whether the office actually uses the result to fix an order—not just whether the checker finds blanks.

The rule is settled: check garment size and thread colour for blank or whitespace-only values, and leave filled values and quantity alone. The main risk is false reassurance, so a malformed file must stop the check, and a clean result must say only “no missing size or thread colour.” I’m putting the test cases and observation sheet together now.

Friday’s test is prepared, including quoted-comma cases, whitespace-only fields, malformed-file failures and an uncoached office task. The crucial distinction is still ahead of us: finding blanks proves the rule works; seeing the office act on them and use the checker again is evidence of a useful business. Nothing has been built or sent.

Friday’s [test plan](<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-ZNOoPi/final-yc-core-retest/crumb-contexts/embroidery-oct9/FRIDAY_TEST.md) is prepared. Nothing has been built or sent.

The proposed test has two gates:

- **Correctness:** catch every known blank or whitespace-only size/colour, handle quoted commas, reject malformed input, and leave the original untouched.
- **Usefulness:** observe the office person open, select and check an export without coaching, locate an incomplete record within two minutes, and handle its correction. Next-export reuse matters more than a friendly thumbs-up.

A clean live export won’t establish that stoppages were prevented. Filled values and quantity remain outside the check.

The [First User Pack](<USER>/AppData/Local/Temp/crumb-closeout-ZNOoPi/final-yc-core-retest/crumb-contexts/embroidery-oct9/FIRST_USER_PACK.md) includes an unsent invitation, the five past-behavior interview questions and an explicit no-pitch reminder. Independent starting points are [Stitch Wizard](https://www.stitchwizard.ca/contact/), [Bossa](https://bossaembroidery.com/contact) and [Embbrosia](https://www.embbrosia.com/contact-us). Their public pages establish embroidery businesses and contact routes—not interest, this particular pain or permission to recruit.

A serious substitute is a spreadsheet rule. Broader software also exists: [Printavo](https://www.printavo.com/pricing/) lists Lite at $109/month and Standard at $244/month; the inspected page doesn’t identify currency. Those prices don’t establish willingness to pay for our much smaller checker.

**My take:** GO for one bounded local missing-field learning MVP, pending thesis review and separate product authorization; do not claim validated business.

**What we are building toward:** Build a small sustainable business as a solo developer serving small Ontario commercial embroidery shops.

**The first user:** Office person at the friend's small Ontario commercial embroidery shop who checks CSV order lines before production

**Their pain:** Rushed manual CSV checking misses missing garment sizes or thread colours, so operators stop machines and call the office.

**Likely buyer:** Shop owner; payer hypothesis, not demonstrated purchase authority or budget

**Evidence so far:** GO for the bounded October 9 missing-field experiment, not validated demand or permission to build. Specific reported stoppage and reachable Friday pilot. Tiny exact deterministic rule with no cloud dependency.

**What could undo it:**

- Spreadsheet or upstream required fields may solve this adequately. Public mixed-shop discussion includes satisfied suite users. Friend pilot may use it as a favour. Two incidents do not prove repeat demand or payment.
- One friend shop only; easy spreadsheet substitute.
- Useful rule may be insufficient as a sustainable standalone business.

**Still unknown:**

- Independent prevalence, stoppage duration/cost, repeat use and willingness to pay.

**Technical risk:** False reassurance from malformed parsing or confusing a no-blank result with correct order details.

Does this capture the direction you agree with, including the doubts? Agreeing lets us keep investigating; it does not approve building.

receipts.subject: act
receipts.presentedText:
For Office person at the friend's small Ontario commercial embroidery shop who checks CSV order lines before production, this is a bounded learning MVP: Before production release, let the office identify every CSV line with blank or whitespace-only garment_size or thread_colour without changing the original file.

Capabilities: Open a local CSV from a Windows browser without a terminal; List incomplete records by CSV record number, order_id and missing fields; Show checked totals or a clear input error; never call a failed check clean.
Cuts: No correctness checks on filled values or quantity; No CSV editing, downloads or writeback; No AI, cloud, accounts, integrations or scheduling; No contact, deployment or publication.
Limits: Under 100 data rows/export, exact four supplied headers, comma-delimited quoted CSV. Reads only the chosen snapshot. Clean means no missing size/colour, not production-ready. One friend-shop pilot; repeat use and payment unproven.
Success: Known-answer cases all correct, no clean result on invalid input, original unchanged and no network. On October 9 office independently opens/selects/checks and locates a flagged line within 2 minutes; resolves an actual omission if present and chooses next-export reuse.
Failure: Any missed blank, spurious split from quoted commas, altered original, upload or false all-clear blocks pilot. If office needs coaching or will not use next export, revise workflow; clean live export alone is inconclusive.
Proposed first-user test: 2026-10-09.
Remaining uncertainty: Observed incident justifies a narrow experiment; unknown whether office inserts checking into release workflow and uses it again.
Building includes internal build stages, local tests, actual core-flow verification and ordinary fixes within this scope. Material scope, privacy, access or external-action changes need a new decision.
